Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: Digital business registry (PPP, supported by NITA and Ministry of Finance) links with eTax portal via API, connects to GRA, NIA databases, and Ghana Post. Online portal for business registration operational. Beneficial ownership register is open and integrated with the company register. TradeNet Services (Singapore-developed) provides electronic trade documentation exchange. Integrations are bilateral/project-based but functionally operational.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: The Ghana Card (NIA) is integrated with multiple systems via bilateral APIs/MoUs: linked to GRA (TIN replaced by Ghana Card PIN, Apr 2021), NHIS, DVLA, business registry, mobile money, banking sector. Integration largely project-based and bilateral rather than through a consolidated national data sharing regime. OpenFn used by Ghana Health Service to generate National IDs for newborns via birth registry integration. ~18 million enrolled as of Oct 2024. Full synchronization still in progress.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: The Electoral Commission (EC) maintains voter registration data independently. The Ghana Card is designed to serve as a single trusted identity including for voting, but EC data and NIA data remain in different formats with no central database linking them. Ghana Card was mandated for SIM registration but electoral integration is incomplete. A 2024 study found data inconsistencies between EC and NIA databases.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: NHIA (National Health Insurance Authority) is one of the five key ID-integrated institutions. Ghana Card is linked to NHIS for waivers - LEAP 1000 program linked Ghana Card to NHIS waivers, improving enrollment by 14-15 percentage points. OpenFn integrates Ghana Health Service with Birth and Death Registry. eCitizen services on Ghana.gov include health-related services. Integration is partially operational across multiple pathways.

Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: DVLA (Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority) is one of the five personal ID-issuing institutions and is noted for bilateral integration with NIA for biometric verification when applying for/renewing driver's licenses. However, DVLA previously refused to join Ghana.gov due to lack of trust and revenue-sharing concerns. Integration is partial/in progress.

Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: The Passport Office is one of the five personal identification issuing institutions studied (alongside NIA, EC, DVLA, NHIA). The Ghana Card is designed for use as e-passport but technical/design challenges persist. Integration with NIA is in progress; passport processing via Ghana Card PIN integration is noted as a challenge (not yet fully progressive in design). Integration is under development.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: GhIPSS (Ghana Interbank Payment and Settlement Systems, est. 2007) provides foundational interoperable payment infrastructure used by all banks, savings/loans companies, mobile money operators, and third-party payment providers. Ghana.gov integrates e-payments for all government services (all MDAs mandated to use it). Payment Systems and Services Act 2019 and Digital Payments Roadmap 2020 provide legal foundation. Financial data exchange is well-established.

Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: GODI (Ghana Open Data Initiative, since 2010) has 315 data catalogs from 22 ministries/agencies under NITA. Ghana Statistical Service provides open data. Beneficial ownership register integrated with company register. Open Government Partnership adopted including at subnational level. Not a unified data exchange but significant open data infrastructure exists.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: GRA eTax portal connects with business registry, NIA databases, and Ghana Post via API. Ghana Card PIN replacing TIN as unique identifier for tax assessment (announced Apr 2021, still transitioning 4 years later). Integration is bilateral/project-based rather than through a unified data exchange hub. eTax portal is operational for e-filing and payments.

Definition: Integration of social assistance programs, grant registries, beneficiary management systems
Comments: GNHR (Ghana National Household Registry) is described as 'Ghana's national hub for social protection data' built for interoperability, enabling secure sharing and system-to-system integration. It provides a centralized household database linked by unique identifiers used by social protection programs. LEAP 1000 program linked Ghana Card to NHIS waivers. Social protection data exchange is functionally operational.

Definition: Whether a detailed implementation roadmap with phases, milestones, and timelines exists for data exchange development
Comments: eGIF (2009) included a roadmap that outlined future legislation and pathways to success, but implementation has been slow with a one-at-a-time approach. The National Data Strategy (2024) includes an implementation roadmap. New bids for a national data exchange hub were issued in 2019 and 2022 but status unclear. eGIF v2.0 is under stakeholder review. Ghana Government Enterprise Architecture Framework (2022) provides implementation process but full roadmap under development.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Comprehensive strategy exists: Ghana Government Enterprise Architecture Framework (2022) provides foundation for data exchange policy implementation. National Data Sharing Policy evolved from National Open Data Action Plan (2011, refreshed multiple times). National Data Strategy validated July 2024 (with Smart Africa, EU, GIZ). Digital Economy Policy & Strategy adopted late 2024. eGIF v2.0 under stakeholder review.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: Ghana has no unified national data exchange hub (eGIF stalled; bid re-issued 2019 and 2022, status unclear). However, several sector-specific data exchange systems are partially operational: Ghana.gov (e-payments portal, all agencies mandated to use it); eTax portal (connects GRA, NIA, Ghana Post via API); GhIPSS (interoperable payment infrastructure used by all banks); GODI (315 data catalogs from 22 agencies). GNHR (national household registry) also enables data sharing for social protection. System is decentralized and partial rather than unified.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: Ghana.gov provides digital services but some critics note it is 'still an elite service'. Ghana Card enrollment of ~18 million out of 34 million (53%) as of Oct 2024 leaves significant population unserved. Ghana ranks 15/47 African countries in 2024 ICT Development Index. Affordability and reliability of access remain concerns. Mobile penetration >135% but data exchange services not universally accessible.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Ghana has a well-established Data Protection Act 2012 (one of 7 African countries compliant with AU Malabo Convention). National Data Sharing Policy covers data licensing and governance. Data Protection Commission enforces compliance. National Data Strategy 2024 addresses data sovereignty. Provisions are relatively strong but enforcement of cross-border data transfer restrictions needs strengthening per 2024 research.

Definition: Whether data exchange infrastructure and services reach rural and remote areas or concentrate in urban centers
Comments: Near-universal broadband (3G/4G) coverage achieved by private sector and government but affordability and reliability remain concerns especially in rural areas. GIFEC created to expand ICT to remote/underserved communities. Ghana Card enrollment in remote areas noted as a challenge needing offline enrollment tools. Data exchange services are primarily urban.
